 Katie Kaplan Tue, October 20, 2026 at 11:36 PM UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. MADISON COUNTY, Iowa-- Residents of Madison County can now breathe a sigh of relief after a months-long delay in property tax statements is reportedly close to an end.
 Auditor Michele Brant confirmed that Madison County tax statements were "uploaded to the outsourcer as of 6 p.m. October 20, 2026."
 The news comes four days after Governor Kim Reynolds issued a strongly worded letter to Treasurer Kylee Barber, and following months of delays by the Treasurer's Office.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement  Ill-fated Ignit Johnston files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy  
 The letter, sent on Friday, read, in part, that "the duration and severity of your office's failure to perform a core, non-discretionary statutory duty involves conduct that is reaching such a level," as potentially leading to action to remove Barber from office. Governor Reynolds set a deadline for Tuesday to have the late statements submitted.
 The delay left local school districts running out of money and local cities forced to secure interest-bearing loans to cover payroll and basic operating expenses.
 It is unclear why property tax statements are delayed or why local entities were not given advance notice of the issue.
 Advertisement Advertisement According to a recent statement Barber provided to WHO 13, applicable penalties on unpaid taxes will be assessed after the 30-day payment period expires, in accordance with county and state requirements.
 Meanwhile, Barber shared emails on Friday that stated she had released the remaining 2025–2026 appropriations. Several cities and school districts confirmed receiving partial payments Friday, but say thousands of dollars in apportionments owed since June remain outstanding.
